intent: Rarely used folders appear on first use; authoring templates move out of browsable folders
notes: A new Gator install no longer creates `threads/`, `policies/` or `field-guides/`, which most repositories never used. Their README and template now ship in `.gator/.includes/<folder>/`, and the constitution tells agents to create the folder from there when someone needs one. User `reference-notes/` works the same way.

No folder people browse holds an authoring template any more (#109). Every `_template.md` (charters, artifacts, procedures, and the on-demand folders) lives in `.gator/.includes/<folder>/`; `README.md` stays where it explains its folder. Install and `gator update` share one placement rule, and an update never puts the old copies back.

`gator update` removes what earlier versions left at the root: every `_template.md`, and an on-demand folder that holds nothing but its README and template. `--dry-run` lists the removals first, a tracked file's deletion is staged, and a folder with real content (for example field guides) keeps it. Gator overwrote these files on every update, so nothing of the user's is lost.
`gator init` no longer counts a README or template as a thread, and shows the working-set line only when threads exist.

The `gator-directory-layout` contract now lists these as on-demand folders, with their templates required in `.gator/.includes/`, and its test asserts that a fresh install creates none of them and leaves no `_template.md` in a browsable folder.

Architect decisions (2026-11-27): remove scaffold-only folders on update, and let agents create on-demand folders from the managed templates (no new command). The blueprint HTML templates stay in `blueprints/` (#96).
